# The direct runtime dependencies, and why each one is here.
#
# This file is the argument; `requirements.lock` is what gets installed. That one
# is generated by `scripts/lock-dependencies.sh`, carries every transitive
# dependency pinned by hash, and is what the image builds from (NFR-SEC-08).
# Editing this file has no effect until the lock is regenerated and committed
# with it.
# Held at the version that pulls a Starlette without the seven advisories the
# dependency audit found against 0.41.3 (NFR-SEC-08). The jump is large because
# the pin was, and the audit is what made that visible.
fastapi==0.141.1
uvicorn[standard]==0.34.0
pydantic==2.10.4
pydantic-settings==2.7.0
sqlalchemy==2.0.36
asyncpg==0.30.0
alembic==1.14.0
redis==5.2.1
structlog==24.4.0

# --- SAML 2.0 (M1) ---------------------------------------------------------
# No libxmlsec1: signxml is pure lxml + cryptography, so the image stays
# multi-arch and the build has no native compilation step. See ADR-003.
lxml==6.1.3
signxml==5.1.0
cryptography==50.0.1
# Required by FastAPI's Form(...) — how POST /saml/acs reads SAMLResponse.
# Its absence fails at route-definition time, not request time.
python-multipart==0.0.32
# Fetching peer metadata: by federation-init now, by the refresh job in M2.
httpx==0.28.1

# --- Directory (M4) --------------------------------------------------------
# ldap3 is pure Python, so the image keeps the no-native-build property that
# ADR-003 chose signxml for. python-ldap would pull in libldap and openldap
# headers and cost the multi-arch build.
#
# It is synchronous, which is deliberate rather than overlooked: the directory
# calls run in a worker thread. An async LDAP client would mean either Twisted
# or a hand-written ASN.1 codec, and neither is a trade this project should
# make for an integration that does one search per login.
ldap3==2.9.1

# --- Second factors (M4) ---------------------------------------------------
# Recovery codes are hashed with Argon2id (FR-MFA-05). Not hand-rolled and not
# substituted: a memory-hard function is the one primitive here whose parameters
# are a security decision rather than an implementation, and getting them wrong
# is invisible until somebody has the database.
#
# It is cffi rather than pure Python, which ADR-003 avoided for signxml. The
# difference is that argon2-cffi publishes manylinux and aarch64 wheels, so the
# image still builds on both architectures with no compiler — the property that
# decision was protecting, rather than the absence of C.
argon2-cffi==23.1.0

# --- Observability (M5) ----------------------------------------------------
# The Prometheus exposition format is a wire format somebody else maintains, and
# getting its escaping, `_total` suffixes or histogram bucket layout subtly wrong
# produces a scrape that looks fine and parses wrong. ADR-003's argument for
# owning the SAML gate was about a *security* boundary; a metrics encoding is
# not one, so this is the library's job. Pure Python, no native build.
prometheus-client==0.21.1

# Tracing (NFR-OBS-02). The API and the SDK, and deliberately none of the
# auto-instrumentation packages: those wrap every database call and every
# outbound request, which produces a trace nobody reads and a dependency on the
# internals of three libraries. The spans here are named by hand at the six
# places a login actually passes through, which is what makes the trace legible.
#
# No exporter package either. Without a configured endpoint the SDK is not
# installed at all and every span is the API's no-op — so a deployment that does
# not want tracing pays nothing for it.
opentelemetry-api==1.44.0
opentelemetry-sdk==1.44.0

# --- OIDC and policy (M2) --------------------------------------------------
# Attribute release policy is declarative YAML (FR-ARP-01). Loaded with
# `safe_load` only — `yaml.load` constructs arbitrary Python objects, which
# turns a policy file into a code-execution surface.
pyyaml==6.0.2
